result.content:
# Proposed discovery plan

Determine whether to develop a dedicated handoff tracker product for small software teams in Latvia.

## Proposed scope

- Assessment of weekly handoff reporting workflows and friction for small Latvian software teams
- Evaluation of integration needs with existing engineering task tracking systems
- Explicit exclusion of payroll processing and financial advisory features

Region: Latvia

Explicit exclusions: Do not include payroll or financial advice

## Engineering Lead

Responsible for sprint coordination, developer handoffs, and operational delivery in small software teams.

- How many hours does your team spend gathering and summarizing weekly handoff information across roles? (question-d6cf5bb15703319803de7bfc)
- What tools do your developers currently use to document and share status changes during weekly handoffs? (question-bb8b9adf4e44a3c712fce9e5)

## Technical Product / Project Manager

Coordinates task tracking, milestone reporting, and cross-functional alignment.

- Under what conditions would you adopt a standalone handoff tracker instead of using existing project management software? (question-da7e109bb37bb024d5303a86)

## Simulation hypotheses

- We spend two hours copying handoff updates each Friday. [source:operator-interview]

## Assumptions

- Small software development teams in Latvia experience recurring manual overhead when consolidating weekly handoffs.
- A dedicated handoff tool could be adopted alongside primary project management suites if friction is sufficiently reduced.

## Evidence gaps

- No empirical data exists regarding market demand or tool willingness-to-pay for development tools exclusively in Latvia.
- Evidence is limited to a single synthetic fixture statement without verified field research.
- No non-synthetic source findings were established; the plan is a proposal, not customer validation.

This scope is proposed, not a claim of user approval.

## Selected sources

- [source:operator-interview] Synthetic operator interview fixture — synthetic_transcript
